While french can be creative when translating movie titles, they kept Matrix the movie by Keanue Reaves. With the popularity of the series, when talking about matrix. The frustration is familiar to malagasy people when people first think about the animated series, lions and zebra, before their island. Matrix, a mathematical object, existed well before the movie series.

A matrix could simply be a way fo storing numbers.

Rabe, Rakoto, Sanda, Dora when to market and here are what they bought
Rabe bought 6 bananas, 3 toko strawberries, and 0.5 kapoaka of voatsinefy.
Rakoto bought 3 bananas, 1 toko of strawberries, no voatsinefy
Sanda bought only 10 toko of strawberries.
Finally, Dora bought 1 banana and 2 kapoaka of vaotsinefy.

This information is arrange in a matrix, each row represents a purchaser, and a column a fruit
$$
\begin{pmatrix}
    6 & 3 & 0.5 \\
    3 & 1 & 0 \\
    0 & 10 & 0 \\
    1 & 0 & 2
\end{pmatrix}
$$

Alternatively, we can structure the data
$$
\begin{pmatrix}
6 & 3 & 0 & 1 \\
3 & 1 & 10 & 0 \\
0.5 & 0 & 0 & 2
\end{pmatrix}
$$

The conversion from the first matrix to the second one is called transposing.

## Formal {.unnumbered}

An $m \times n$ matrix is a rectangular array of elements in a set $\Omega$ having m rows and n columns. It is denoted as:

$$
A =
\begin{pmatrix}
    a_{11} & a_{12} & \dots & a_{1n} \\
    a_{21} & a_{22} & \dots & a_{2n} \\
    \vdots & \vdots & & \vdots \\
    a_{m1} & a_{m2} & \dots & a_{mn}
\end{pmatrix}
$$

where the element $a_{i,j} \in \Omega $ denotes the entry in the ith row and jth column of A. The domain of the row index i is {1,2,…,m} and the domain of the column index j is {1,2,…,n}. $\Omega$ could be natural or real number or anything else.

In mathematics, a vector is special case of matrix, consisting of with one column.

## Examples {.unnumbered}

- As square matrix is with the same number of row and column

$$
\begin{pmatrix}
6 & 3 & 0 \\
3 & 1 & 10 \\
0.5 & 0 & 0
\end{pmatrix}
$$

- A diagonal matrix has all element of the diagonal equals to 0, it is often noted diag()
$$
\begin{pmatrix}
a & 0 & 0 \\
0 & b & 0 \\
0 & 0 & c
\end{pmatrix}
$$

- A matrix can be symmetric where the values are the same the diagonal, ie $a_{i,j} = a_{j,i}$
$$
\begin{pmatrix}
a & 1 & x \\
1 & b & -1 \\
x & -1 & c
\end{pmatrix}
$$

## Tips and warning {.unnumbered}
- Semantic: element, entry,
- A matrix is often denoted by a capital letter, sometimes in bold to differentiate from value which are mostly lower case.
- A community matrix for ecologist have the number of species per site
- A distance matrix is a square and symmetric matrix computed after say community matrix. Each element is pairwise distance between two sites. Since distance between site A and site B is the same as the distance between site B and site A. The element on the diagonal is the distance between the same site and could be 0 or 1 depending on the distance represent similarity or dissimilarity.
- From a mathematical matrix, a column matrix is different than a row matrix (1 x n) is not the same as (n x 1) although one can transpose it.
- Matrix is more than a rectangle storing data, it is the foundation of linear algebra...and sometimes have magical properties. Maybe in future chapters
- A [data frame](@sec-dataframe) is also a rectangular object mostly used in data-science. The columns could be a different type (numbers, text, etc.). There is no equivalent of data frame in mathematics.
- The huge field of linear algebra in mathematics is essentially understand the properties of matrix.
